text:
maya: Quick flag 1: our weekly playbook sweep bumped 320 accounts into 'low-engagement' overnight. AMs are seeing tickets. Preliminary sample shows many accounts have `do_not_track=true` (consent cookie) and also have recent email opens. Playbook currently treats missing telemetry as inactive.

leo: I pulled a random sample of 200 flagged accounts. 64% have recent email_open events in `marketing.events`. So telemetry missing != inactive. We should add a secondary signal chain: email_open OR crm_manual_touch OR last_web_session.

cs-ops-bot: playbook-run 3123456789 completed 02:12:07 flagged=320 signals_missing=198 (:warning:)

hana: Suggestion: introduce a "grace window" where absence of `page_ping` for <=7d and presence of email_open within 14d => treat as active. That avoids flipping accounts that opted out of analytics.

carl (data): I can add a derived column `engagement_backup` in the daily materialized view:

```
-- pseudo
engagement_backup = (email_open_ts >= now()-14d) OR (crm_touch_ts >= now()-30d) OR (last_web_session >= now()-7d)
```

Then scorer can prefer `max(event_ts, engagement_backup_ts)` when computing recency. I'll run a dry recalculation for a cohort.

anya: Also, we should avoid changing scoring logic without a dry-run gate. Proposed plan: 1) add `engagement_backup` field and a flag `use_backup=false` by default 2) run dry-run over `q3-onboard` cohort and compare label churn 3) if stable, enable `use_backup=true` and canary to 10% prod.

sam (product): Agree. Also add a toggle in the CS console so CS Ops can flip `use_backup` for emergency fixes. We don't want code deploys for quick mitigations.

maya: Who can run the dry-run and produce delta CSV (acct_id, old_score, new_score, backup_reason)? Ideally include `consent_status` and `email_open_ts`.

carl (data): I will. Running command:

```
./bin/score --cohort q3-onboard --dry-run --patch=eng_backup --out s3://redwood-cs/dryruns/3123456789/eng_backup.csv --sample 1k
```

ETA ~20m. Will include counts and sample rows.

leo: Heads-up for AMs: please mute the healthscore anomaly alerts tagged `playbook-dryrun` for the next hour. They'll be noisy. @maya can you pause them?

maya: Paused healthscore alerts for tag=playbook-dryrun until 3123458200.

cs-ops-bot: alerts muted by maya until 3123458200 (:white_check_mark:)

hana: Small UX ask: when `engagement_backup` is used to keep an account active, surface the reason in the UI under "why active" so AMs can see "email_open: 2026-09-18" rather than guessing.

sam (product): Will add a small field `backup_reason` to the account summary card. Low effort.

carl (data): Dry-run finished. Summary: sample=1000, flagged_before=320, flagged_after=48, major_reduction driven by email_open hits (412 of 672 previously missing telemetry had email opens). Uploaded CSV: s3://redwood-cs/dryruns/3123456789/eng_backup.csv

cs-ops-bot: dry-run 3123456789 results posted (s3://redwood-cs/dryruns/3123456789/eng_backup.csv) (:chart_with_upwards_trend:)

leo: Those numbers look great. FP reduced substantially. Next steps: stage rollout + UI toggle + staging smoke.

anya: I'll open config PR to add `playbook.engagement.use_backup` default=false and add a canary rollout plan. PR: https://git.redwood/s/cs/config/+/4021

maya: Also craft AM message explaining root cause: consent opt-outs suppress telemetry; we added fallback signals (email opens and CRM touches) and will rerun playbook for impacted accounts tonight. I'll attach the CSV.

sam (product): One more thing: let's add a regression test in CI that simulates `do_not_track=true` and asserts `engagement_backup` picks up email_open. Prevents accidental regressions.

carl (data): Adding the test now.

maya: Thanks team. If staging run looks good let's flip `use_backup` for 10% tomorrow morning and monitor alert rates and AM feedback for 24h. I'll collect AM responses after the rerun. Appreciate the quick turnaround :heart:
